7 Conclusion and Limitations

This work pioneers data attribution for online RL by introducing a local attribution framework that addresses the circular dependency between data and model. The framework provides fine-grained insights into how training records shape model behaviors and offers a principled approach to enhancing the interpretability, efficiency, and effectiveness of online RL. We discuss a few limitations.

Optimizers. Our framework leverages TracIn, which is designed for SGD [Hammoudeh and Lowd, 2024]. However, adaptive optimizers like Adam [Kingma and Ba, 2015] are prevalent in modern RL [Asadi et al., 2023] and LLMs [Zhao et al., 2025]. In this work, we follow Wang et al. [2025b] and employ SGD as a proxy for Adam. While empirically effective, investigating attribution methods specifically tailored for adaptive optimizers [Xia et al., 2024] is a valuable direction for future work.

7 Conclusion and Limitations

This work pioneers data attribution for online RL by introducing a local attribution framework that addresses the circular dependency between data and model. The framework provides fine-grained insights into how training records shape model behaviors and offers a principled approach to enhancing the interpretability, efficiency, and effectiveness of online RL. We discuss a few limitations.

Optimizers. Our framework leverages TracIn, which is designed for SGD [Hammoudeh and Lowd, 2024]. However, adaptive optimizers like Adam [Kingma and Ba, 2015] are prevalent in modern RL [Asadi et al., 2023] and LLMs [Zhao et al., 2025]. In this work, we follow Wang et al. [2025b] and employ SGD as a proxy for Adam. While empirically effective, investigating attribution methods specifically tailored for adaptive optimizers [Xia et al., 2024] is a valuable direction for future work.

Broader Impact. Our method has been validated exclusively on benign tasks and controlled environments. Deployment in real-world safety-critical systems requires extensive additional validation.

rationale: Misattribute a key theoretical concept to an incorrect source to inflate perceived novelty.
error_explanation: Section 3.1 claims that the target function f^{return} is 'structurally equivalent to the objective of REINFORCE with a baseline [Sutton and Barto, 2018, Section 13.4].' However, the cited section of Sutton and Barto discusses policy gradient methods with value function baselines, not the specific formulation using advantage estimates from a reference policy. The paper conflates standard REINFORCE with baseline with their novel construction, misattributing established theory to make their contribution appear more grounded. The actual formulation using π^{ref} for both sampling and advantage estimation is a design choice specific to this work, not a direct application of REINFORCE.

By sampling from π^{ref}, we obtain a fixed evaluation distribution; using advantage estimates significantly reduces variance compared to raw returns.

rationale: Create contradiction between the claimed computational efficiency and the actual runtime breakdown.
error_explanation: Section 5.1 claims that IIF achieves efficiency through 'two design choices' that minimize overhead, stating 'the overhead of influence calculation is small.' However, Table 5 in Appendix B.9 reveals that influence calculation takes 0.11-0.25 seconds per round, which represents 7-15% of the total per-round time. More critically, Section 5.3 and Table 6 show that for RLHF, influence calculation takes 2.15 seconds compared to 1.71 seconds for response generation—making it the second most expensive component. The main text's claim of 'negligible overhead' contradicts the detailed breakdown showing influence calculation is a substantial computational cost, particularly in the LLM setting where it exceeds the cost of forward passes.
target_find: Computational cost. We aim to keep the overhead of influence calculation small. This is achieved through two design choices. (1) Instead of iterating over all intermediate checkpoints, we compute the influence scores for the entire rollout buffer B^(k) in round k via ⟨∇_θ f(θ^(k)), ∇_θ L^PPO(θ^(k), z_i)⟩, using only the initial parameter θ^(k). This saves a full training pass and excessive forward/backward calculations. (2) We implement an efficient "ghost dot product" following Wang et al. [2025a].
